thread:
Anna K: quick check — packing the Node/TS SDK for Next/Vercel edge and hitting a few surprises with auth + streaming. bundling target is 'edge' in next.config, but when I import the normal entrypoint I see `ReferenceError: crypto is not defined` during build and then streaming hangs at runtime.

Anna K: example client init i'm using:```js
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY })
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ messages: [...] })
for await (const chunk of stream) { /* handle */ }
```

Anna K: works fine in node dev, fails when built for edge. wondering if we should recommend a separate edge entrypoint or document polyfills. pinging @Josh M because you landed some bundler changes last week.

Josh M: ah yeah this is a common mixup. two things: 1) the default node entry expects Node webcrypto, 2) some bundlers rewrite globalThis/Buffer causing streaming helpers to break. we have an `edge` entry in the SDK but it isn't advertised well. try `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` — that one avoids node-specific shims.

Priya S: fwiw on Vercel edge you should not polyfill `crypto` — the runtime provides Web Crypto. the error you saw is during the build step when esbuild/webpack tries to resolve `require('crypto')`. recommend marking node-only modules as external in the edge build or use conditional exports.

Liam W: another workaround if you must use the same bundle: in next.config.js add webpack fallback to ignore `crypto` for edge:```js
webpack: (config, { isServer }) => {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'edge') {
    config.resolve.fallback = { crypto: false }
  }
  return config
}
```
This prevents the bundler from inlining a node crypto stub that breaks runtime.

Anna K: thanks. streaming hang still puzzling — responses start, then stop mid-stream with no error. logs show chunk loop never resumes.

Josh M: check that the SDK's streaming helper uses the global ReadableStream and not polyfilled Node streams. Edge expects WHATWG streams. if you accidentally include the Node stream polyfill, the `for await` may not consume correctly. our edge entrypoint switches to `response.body.getReader()` under the hood.

Priya S: also check headers: Vercel strips some connection headers; ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and `Content-Type: text/event-stream` are preserved. sometimes a proxy will buffer until a certain size and then flush, making it look like it stalled.

Anna K: good call. i'll try edge entrypoint + confirm headers. I'll open a tiny repro later.

Liam W: if you open a repro ping me i can quick-run it on the preview. also let's add a short blurb in the SDK README: "Edge runtimes: import from 'redwood-inference/edge' and avoid node polyfills" — saves future headaches.

Anna K: filed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 — adds docs + a conditional export for /edge entry. could use a quick CR.

Josh M: looking now. small nit: update package.json exports to have explicit './edge': './dist/edge/index.js' so bundlers pick it reliably.

Priya S: +1 to explicit export. also add a test in ci matrix that builds for a Vite edge target to catch regressions.

ci-bot: all checks passed for branch edge-entry-docs (CI \u2014 build + unit + e2e) :white_check_mark:

Anna K: sweet, thanks team. i'll merge on green and follow up with the repro results in this thread. :thumbsup:
